key_facts: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang quit as chief executive after reports of alleged extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset, Alice Huang (no relation), who worked at the Singaporean firm Megaspeed; a second reported relationship was with long-time Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell.

Nvidia lost $550bn (£415bn) in stock market value in five days; the stock fell 31% from its recent peak, the largest five-day drop since the company went public 27 years ago. Nvidia's value is about 7% of the S&P 500.

CFO Colette Kress was named interim CEO; Nvidia is searching for a permanent replacement. US Attorney General Todd Blanche said the Justice Department had not yet drawn conclusions on whether Alice Huang engaged in espionage for Beijing; China rejected the allegations as a smear. Senators Warren and Coons and House Democrats demanded Huang brief Congress.
importance_reason: Leadership exit at one of the world's most valuable AI chipmakers with a $550bn five-day market-cap loss and a national-security dimension, though the underlying espionage claims remain unconfirmed.
market_link: Sharp drop in Nvidia shares affects AI-sector valuations and, via its ~7% weight, the S&P 500 and US index-fund retirement accounts; leadership uncertainty may weigh on the chip supply chain and AI-related equities.

key_facts: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick reportedly took a softer line on Nvidia's advanced AI chip sales than other senior Trump administration officials, who broadly favor tighter controls to keep China from using the chips in the AI race.

Over the past year, Lutnick has frequently clashed with top officials over how to regulate advanced technology sales, particularly Nvidia's chip sales to Asia; critics in the administration and Congress say the Commerce Department is too cozy with Nvidia and co-founder Jensen Huang and has not adequately policed chip sales to China.

The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang was in a relationship with Alice Huang, a top executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, which is suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips to China; U.S. intelligence agencies reportedly believe she is a Chinese spy. Jensen Huang announced he was stepping down from Megaspeed, and the company's shares fell sharply.

Lutnick, as head of the department that enforces technology sales restrictions, is positioned to largely shape whether China gets access to American technology; within Commerce, Nvidia reportedly receives different treatment, with its issues given high priority and routed through specific channels.

A highly classified memo on concerns about Alice Huang and Megaspeed was shared with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who reportedly resisted action against the company. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent reportedly questioned why Megaspeed had not been placed on the Commerce Department's blacklist. Congressional Democrats have opened an investigation into how Commerce vetted Chinese companies approved to buy AI chips; Republicans, including Rep. John Moolenaar and Sen. Elizabeth Warren (Democrat), are also pressing the administration. Huang's team told Republican lawmakers he plans to cooperate with a closed-door testimony request. key_facts: Microsoft said it is "deeply sorry" for a global outage affecting Outlook, Teams and other Microsoft 365 products; services were broadly recovering by Friday afternoon, nearly 24 hours after issues began.

The outage hit more than 70 countries; more than 430 million people use the affected products worldwide. Microsoft attributed the problem to a technical issue introduced during a "network capacity upgrade", stating it was not related to cyber or AI agents.

Affected sectors included government institutions (Japanese government, Philippines Supreme Court, Australian spy agency), NHS parts, schools, police forces, Canadian rail and hospitals, and the US House of Representatives, which said a full day of legislative work was set back.

Microsoft first acknowledged the problem at 17:54 GMT on Thursday; at 04:36 on Friday it reported only partial recovery, and by 13:32 it reported broader improvements in North America and sustained improvements in Europe. Full post-incident report is pending.
importance_reason: Major operational disruption to a widely used service, but no direct market, macro or price effect is reported in the article.
